BetaTargetStoreHeldError.description:
Returned with status 409 when a request to create a dream sets `output_behavior` to `update_existing` and another dream that writes into the same memory store hasn't fully stopped.

The other dream is `pending` or `running`, or it has just stopped and is still finishing its last writes. `message` gives the ID of the other dream when the server can identify it. If that dream has already reached `completed`, `failed`, or `canceled`, retry after a short wait. Otherwise, wait for the other dream to end or cancel it, then retry. The response sets the `x-should-retry` header to `false`.

message.description: A human-readable explanation of why the memory store can't be used yet, with the ID of the dream that is using it when the server can identify it.

BetaTelemetryDestination.description: An OpenTelemetry destination: an OTLP/HTTP endpoint, the request headers sent with every delivery to it, what the exported spans contain, and which workspaces it covers. A destination belongs to an organization. A workspace's spans go to every enabled destination that covers it.

id.description: The unique ID of the destination (`tdst_...`).

display_name.description: Human-readable name for the destination. Null when none was set.

endpoint_url.description:
The base URL of the destination's OTLP/HTTP endpoint, exactly as registered.

The API appends the per-signal path, such as `/v1/traces`, on delivery, unless `traces.endpoint_url` is set.

header_names.description: Names of the registered request headers. Header values are write-only and are never returned.

traces.description: The destination's settings for the traces it receives.

delivery_health.description: The most recent delivery results for this destination.

created_at.description: Time the destination was created.

updated_at.description:
Time of the last change to the destination's configuration or state. Changes to `delivery_health` don't change it.

An update that sets a header value always changes it, even when the value is the same as before. Adding or removing a single workspace on the destination's list doesn't change it. An update that changes the list does.

workspaces.description: Which of the organization's workspaces the destination covers.

BetaTelemetryDestinationContentMode.description:
What the spans that the API exports to a telemetry destination contain.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry#choose-a-content-mode) to learn what the spans contain in each content mode.
x-enum-descriptions: The spans contain identifiers, timing, status, token counts, and similar metadata. They don't contain prompt text, completion text, or tool inputs and outputs.

The spans contain the same metadata as `metadata_only`, plus message and tool content.

An organization with a data-handling restriction, such as under HIPAA, can't choose this mode. The API exports only metadata for such an organization, even to a destination that already has `content`.

BetaTelemetryDestinationDeliveryHealth.description:
The most recent delivery results that the API records for a telemetry destination.

Changes to the destination's configuration or state don't reset these fields. Changes to these fields don't change `updated_at`. The values can lag behind the latest deliveries.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry#delivery-and-health) to learn how the API delivers spans and when it disables a destination.

last_success_at.description: Time of the most recent successful delivery to the destination, or `null` if no delivery has succeeded yet.

last_error.description:
A message that describes the most recent failed delivery to the destination, or `null` if no delivery has failed yet.

Examples are `temporary DNS failure`, `TLS failure`, `timeout`, `connection failure`, `invalid address`, `HTTP error (status 503)`, and `redirect (status 301)`. The message is `invalid address` both for a hostname that doesn't exist and for an address that isn't publicly routable. It never contains the endpoint's response body, a header value, a network address, or TLS details.

`last_error` and `last_error_at` always change together. A later successful delivery doesn't clear them. If `last_success_at` is later than `last_error_at`, a delivery has succeeded since this failure.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry#delivery-errors) to learn the likely cause of each error.

last_error_at.description: Time of the failure that `last_error` describes. Changes together with `last_error`. Null until a delivery first fails.

BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReason.description: Why the destination is disabled: `caller` when a caller disabled it, or the reason the API disabled it automatically (`sustained_failure`, `invalid_address`, or `redirect`). Every automatic disable is reversible with an update that sets `state` to `enabled`. An update that sets `disabled` on a destination that is already disabled keeps its reason.

BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonCa.description: A caller disabled the destination with an update that set `state` to `disabled`.

BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonIn.description: The API disabled the destination because deliveries to it failed for longer than the same threshold as for `sustained_failure`, and the most recent failed delivery failed with an invalid address: the DNS answer says that the endpoint's hostname doesn't exist or doesn't have an address, or the address that the API would connect to isn't publicly routable or is reserved, for example a loopback, link-local, private-network, or cloud-metadata address. The API doesn't connect to such an address, and retries the delivery a bounded number of times as it does after a timeout. A timeout or a server failure of the DNS lookup is a temporary DNS failure instead, not an invalid address.

BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonRe.description: The API disabled the destination because the endpoint answered a delivery with a 3xx status. Redirects are never followed, and one such answer disables the destination at once.

BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonSu.description: The API disabled the destination because deliveries to it failed, with no successful delivery in between, for longer than a threshold that Anthropic configures and that is not part of this contract. The reason is `invalid_address` instead when the most recent failed delivery failed with an invalid address.

BetaTelemetryDestinationState.description:
Whether a telemetry destination receives deliveries.

A caller can set either state. The API also disables an enabled destination on its own in some cases. The `reason` of the disabled state says whether a caller or the API disabled the destination and, when the API did, why.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry#delivery-and-health) to learn when the API disables a destination.

BetaTelemetryDestinationStateDisabled.description:
The API doesn't deliver anything to the telemetry destination.

Spans produced while it is disabled aren't delivered later.

reason.description: Whether a caller or the API disabled the destination and, when the API did, why. Read-only.

BetaTelemetryDestinationStateDisabledPar.description:
Stop deliveries to the telemetry destination.

Spans produced while it is disabled aren't delivered later. A destination that is already disabled keeps its `reason`.

BetaTelemetryDestinationStateEnabled.description: The telemetry destination receives the spans of the workspaces that it covers.

BetaTelemetryDestinationStateEnabledPara.description:
Start deliveries to the telemetry destination again.

This doesn't reset `delivery_health`.

BetaTelemetryDestinationStateParams.description:
The state to set on a telemetry destination, by `type` alone.

A caller can't set the `reason` of a disabled state. Only the API sets it.

BetaTelemetryDestinationTest.description: The result of one test span sent to a destination.

result.description: How the test went: `success` when the destination answered with a 2xx status, else `failure` with the reason.

BetaTelemetryDestinationTestFailure.description: The test span was not delivered.

error.description: A message that describes why the test span was not delivered, including the HTTP status code when the destination returned one. Examples: `HTTP error (status 403)`, `timeout`, `TLS failure`. It has the same form as the destination's `delivery_health.last_error` and never contains the destination's response body, any header value, a network address, or TLS details.

BetaTelemetryDestinationTestResult.description: The outcome of a test: `success`, or `failure` with the reason.

BetaTelemetryDestinationTestSuccess.description: The destination answered the test span with a 2xx status.

BetaTelemetryDestinationTraces.description: A telemetry destination's settings for the traces it receives.

enabled.description: Whether the destination receives traces. A destination whose `enabled` is false keeps its other settings.

endpoint_url.description:
The full URL that the API posts traces to, exactly as registered, or `null` if the destination doesn't have one.

When it is `null`, the API posts traces to `endpoint_url` with `/v1/traces` appended.

max_content_bytes.description:
The most bytes of content that one exported span can contain, or `null` if only the API's maximum applies.

Content means model prompts and responses, and tool inputs and outputs. The API shortens longer content to this size before it delivers the span. A destination whose `content_mode` is `metadata_only` keeps this value. It applies once `content_mode` is `content`.

BetaTelemetryDestinationTracesParams.description: The settings for the traces that a telemetry destination receives, as a create or update request sets them. An omitted field takes its default on create and keeps its stored value on update.

enabled.description: Whether the destination receives traces. Defaults to true on create. It cannot be null.

endpoint_url.description:
The full URL of your collector's traces endpoint, for a collector that takes traces on a path other than `/v1/traces`. The API posts traces to it exactly as given and appends nothing.

The same rules as for `endpoint_url` apply, except that any path is allowed. It must have the same scheme, host, and port as `endpoint_url`. At most 2,048 characters.

On create, `null` is the same as leaving it out. On update, `null` removes it. The API then posts traces to `endpoint_url` with `/v1/traces` appended. A change of this URL alone keeps the registered headers.

content_mode.description:
What the exported spans contain. Defaults to `metadata_only` on create.

On update, `null` sets `metadata_only`.

max_content_bytes.description:
The most bytes of content that one exported span can contain, from 1 up to the API's maximum. `null` sets no bound, so only the API's maximum applies.

On create, leaving it out is the same as `null`. The error for a value above the maximum states the maximum.

BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspace.description:
A workspace on a telemetry destination's workspace list.

Under `include`, the destination covers the workspace. Under `exclude`, the destination covers every workspace except this one. The entry doesn't have an `id`. Its `telemetry_destination_id` and `workspace_id` together identify it.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace (`wrkspc_...`).

created_at.description: Time the workspace was added to the list.

BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspaces.description:
Which of the organization's workspaces a telemetry destination covers.

Several destinations can cover the same workspace. Each of them receives the workspace's spans while it is enabled.

The workspace list of an `include` or `exclude` destination isn't part of the destination object. List the destination's workspaces to read it. Add or remove one workspace at a time, or replace the whole list with an update. A list holds at most 1,000 workspaces.

BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesAll.description: The destination covers every workspace of the organization, including the default workspace, archived workspaces, and workspaces created later. It doesn't have a list.

BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesAllPar.description:

reason.description:
Which binding check removed the block: `model_binding_mismatch` — it was
created by a model whose reasoning the requested model may not read;
`prefix_binding_mismatch` — the conversation before it differs from the
conversation it was created in (the rest of that turn's consecutive thinking
blocks are removed with it, each with this reason);
`organization_binding_mismatch` — it was created under a different
organization (an Anthropic organization, AWS account or Google Cloud project)
and this organization is not one of its additional organizations;
`end_user_binding_mismatch` — it was created for a different end user, or
was removed by the consumer-organization binding. A block that would fail
several checks reports one reason, in this order of precedence:
`organization_binding_mismatch`, `end_user_binding_mismatch`,
`model_binding_mismatch`, `prefix_binding_mismatch`.

endpoint_url.description:
The new base URL of the destination's OTLP/HTTP endpoint. The same rules as on create apply.

A change of hostname or port first removes every registered header, so send the headers for the new endpoint in the same request. When the destination has a `traces.endpoint_url`, such a change must also set `traces.endpoint_url` to a URL with the new hostname and port, or to `null`. A change of the path alone keeps the headers.

headers.description:
Headers to set or remove. The API merges them into the destination's headers by name.

Names compare case-insensitively. A string value sets or replaces that header. A `null` value removes it. Headers that you omit don't change. The field itself can't be `null`.

A request that sets a header value must also include `endpoint_url`. The current URL is accepted.

The resulting set must stay within the same limits as on create. When the request sets a value, each stored value that it doesn't set counts as 4,096 bytes toward the 16,384-byte limit, because you can't read its real length. So to change one header of a destination that has four or more other headers, send the values of the others again in the same request.

traces.description:
The traces settings to change. Omitted settings keep their stored values.

`null` sets every traces setting to its create default.

state.description: Whether the destination receives deliveries after the update. The field can't be `null`.

workspaces.description:
The new workspace scope, in the same form as on create. The field can't be `null`.

The API refuses an update that changes the type or sends `workspace_ids` while the destination's list has more than 750 workspaces. Remove workspaces one at a time until 750 or fewer remain, then send the update again.

prompt.description:
The prompt that you want Claude to complete.

For proper response generation you will need to format your prompt using alternating `\n\nHuman:` and `\n\nAssistant:` conversational turns. For example:

```
"\n\nHuman: {userQuestion}\n\nAssistant:"
```

See [prompt validation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/working-with-messages) and our guide to [prompt design](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview) for more details.
prompt.title: Prompt

max_tokens_to_sample.description:
The maximum number of tokens to generate before stopping.

Note that our models may stop _before_ reaching this maximum. This parameter only specifies the absolute maximum number of tokens to generate.
max_tokens_to_sample.title: Max Tokens To Sample

stop_sequences.description:
Sequences that will cause the model to stop generating.

Our models stop on `"\n\nHuman:"`, and may include additional built-in stop sequences in the future. By providing the stop_sequences parameter, you may include additional strings that will cause the model to stop generating.
stop_sequences.title: Stop Sequences

temperature.description:
Amount of randomness injected into the response.

Defaults to `1.0`. Ranges from `0.0` to `1.0`. Use `temperature` closer to `0.0` for analytical / multiple choice, and closer to `1.0` for creative and generative tasks.

Note that even with `temperature` of `0.0`, the results will not be fully deterministic.
temperature.title: Temperature
temperature.x-stainless-deprecation-message: Deprecated. Models released after Claude Opus 4.6 do not support setting temperature. A value of 1.0 will be accepted for backwards compatibility, all other values will be rejected with a 400 error.

top_p.description:
Use nucleus sampling.

In nucleus sampling, we compute the cumulative distribution over all the options for each subsequent token in decreasing probability order and cut it off once it reaches a particular probability specified by `top_p`.

Recommended for advanced use cases only.
top_p.title: Top P
top_p.x-stainless-deprecation-message: Deprecated. Models released after Claude Opus 4.6 do not support setting top_p. A value >= 0.99 will be accepted for backwards compatibility, all other values will be rejected with a 400 error.

top_k.description:
Only sample from the top K options for each subsequent token.

Used to remove "long tail" low probability responses. [Learn more technical details here](https://towardsdatascience.com/how-to-sample-from-language-models-682bceb97277).

Recommended for advanced use cases only.
top_k.title: Top K
top_k.x-stainless-deprecation-message: Deprecated. Models released after Claude Opus 4.6 do not accept top_k; any value will be rejected with a 400 error.

messages.description:
Input messages.

Our models are trained to operate on alternating `user` and `assistant` conversational turns. When creating a new `Message`, you specify the prior conversational turns with the `messages` parameter, and the model then generates the next `Message` in the conversation. Consecutive `user` or `assistant` turns in your request will be combined into a single turn.

Each input message must be an object with a `role` and `content`. You can specify a single `user`-role message, or you can include multiple `user` and `assistant` messages.

If the final message uses the `assistant` role, the response content will continue immediately from the content in that message. This can be used to constrain part of the model's response. This is called prefill. On models that don't support prefill, creating a message that ends with a partial `assistant` response returns a 400 error. See [Prefill not supported](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#prefill-not-supported).

Example with a single `user` message:

```json
[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello, Claude"}]
```

Example with multiple conversational turns:

```json
[
  {"role": "user", "content": "Hello there."},
  {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi, I'm Claude. How can I help you?"},
  {"role": "user", "content": "Can you explain LLMs in plain English?"},
]
```

Example with a partially-filled response from Claude, for models that support prefill:

```json
[
  {"role": "user", "content": "What's the Greek name for Sun? (A) Sol (B) Helios (C) Sun"},
  {"role": "assistant", "content": "The best answer is ("},
]
```

Each input message `content` may be either a single `string` or an array of content blocks, where each block has a specific `type`. Using a `string` for `content` is shorthand for an array of one content block of type `"text"`. The following input messages are equivalent:

```json
{"role": "user", "content": "Hello, Claude"}
```

```json
{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Hello, Claude"}]}
```

See [input examples](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/working-with-messages).

Note that if you want to include a [system prompt](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#give-claude-a-role), you can use the top-level `system` parameter.

There is a limit of 100,000 messages in a single request.

Custom text sequences that will cause the model to stop generating.

Our models will normally stop when they have naturally completed their turn, which will result in a response `stop_reason` of `"end_turn"`.

content.description:
Content generated by the model.

This is an array of content blocks, each of which has a `type` that determines its shape.

Example:

```json
[{"type": "text", "text": "Hi, I'm Claude."}]
```

If the request input `messages` ended with an `assistant` turn, then the response `content` will continue directly from that last turn. You can use this to constrain the model's output.

For example, if the input `messages` were:
```json
[
  {"role": "user", "content": "What's the Greek name for Sun? (A) Sol (B) Helios (C) Sun"},
  {"role": "assistant", "content": "The best answer is ("}
]
```

Then the response `content` might be:

```json
[{"type": "text", "text": "B)"}]
```

stop_reason.description:
The reason that we stopped.

This may be one the following values:
* `"end_turn"`: the model reached a natural stopping point
* `"max_tokens"`: we exceeded the requested `max_tokens` or the model's maximum
* `"stop_sequence"`: one of your provided custom `stop_sequences` was generated
* `"tool_use"`: the model invoked one or more tools
* `"pause_turn"`: we paused a long-running turn. You may provide the response back as-is in a subsequent request to let the model continue.
* `"refusal"`: when streaming classifiers intervene to handle potential policy violations
* `"model_context_window_exceeded"`: we exceeded the model's context window

In non-streaming mode this value is always non-null. In streaming mode, it is null in the `message_start` event and non-null otherwise.

usage.description:
Billing and rate-limit usage.

Anthropic's API bills and rate-limits by token counts, as tokens represent the underlying cost to our systems.

Under the hood, the API transforms requests into a format suitable for the model. The model's output then goes through a parsing stage before becoming an API response. As a result, the token counts in `usage` will not match one-to-one with the exact visible content of an API request or response.

For example, `output_tokens` will be non-zero, even for an empty string response from Claude.

Total input tokens in a request is the summation of `input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, and `cache_read_input_tokens`.

UserProfile.description:
A record of an entity that the platform serves through the API, such as an end-user of the platform's product or a company that the platform resells Claude access to.

A Messages, Message Batches or token counting request can send a profile's `id` in the `anthropic-user-profile-id` header to attribute the request to that entity.

id.description: Unique identifier for this user profile, prefixed `uprof_`.

type.description: Object type. Always `user_profile`.

name.description: Real-world name of the entity this profile represents (company or individual). For a company the platform resells Claude access to (`access_type` `passthrough`) this is that company's name. `null` until the platform supplies one.

access_type.description: How the platform uses the API for this entity: `application` (default) or `passthrough`. Absent under the legacy `user-profiles-2026-03-24` beta header.

external_user_details.description: Details about the entity this profile represents, as the platform states them; not verified by Anthropic. Every field is present, `null` until the platform supplies a value. Absent under the legacy `user-profiles-2026-03-24` and `user-profiles-2026-08-18` beta headers, which serve `reference_id` as the top-level `external_id` and, under `user-profiles-2026-08-18`, `onboarded_at` as `external_user_onboarded_at`.

enforcement_status.description: Anthropic's enforcement status of this profile, from its open enforcement actions and any identity check under review, by the first rule that applies: `banned` while any open action is a `ban`; `pending` while a restriction that an identity check can clear is open, the end user has submitted that check, Anthropic's review of it has not ended, and no open action's `reason` is `account_compromise`; `restricted` while any action is open; `unrestricted` while none is. Absent under the `user-profiles-2026-09-04` and earlier beta headers.

enforcement_actions.description: The enforcement actions open on this profile; empty when none is open. Absent under the `user-profiles-2026-09-04` and earlier beta headers.

programs.description: The profile's standing in each Anthropic program, such as the Cyber Verification Program. Present when the request sends no user-profiles beta header; absent under the `user-profiles-2026-09-04` and earlier beta headers, which serve `trust_grants` instead.

created_at.description: When this user profile was created, in RFC 3339 format.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata. Maximum 16 pairs, keys up to 64 chars, values up to 512 chars.

updated_at.description: When this user profile was last modified, in RFC 3339 format. It normally also updates shortly after Anthropic gives the profile an approval or withdraws one. Other changes to the statuses that Anthropic reports do not always update it, so read the status itself rather than watching this timestamp.

UserProfileAccessType.description: How the platform uses the API on behalf of the entity this profile represents. `application`: the platform sells a product that uses the API behind the scenes, and the profile represents an individual end-user of that product. `passthrough`: the platform resells raw inference, and the profile identifies the resold-to company.
x-enum-descriptions: The user profile represents an individual end-user of a product that the platform builds on the API. New profiles get this value by default.
The user profile represents a company that the platform resells Claude access to.

UserProfileAction.description: The action that the person who opens the URL takes, discriminated by `type`.

UserProfileActionUrl.description: A URL to give to the person who takes the requested action.

type.description: Object type. Always `user_profile_action_url`.

url.description: The URL to give to the person who takes the action. Anyone who holds it can open it until `expires_at`.

expires_at.description: When the URL stops working, in RFC 3339 format.

UserProfileCyberProgram.description: A user profile's standing in the Cyber Verification Program, which relaxes cyber safeguards for requests that name the profile.

status.description: `active` when at least one tier is `active`, or when the profile has the program's access to earlier models. That access is not a tier: a profile that has it alone reads `active` with every tier `inactive`, or with `tiers` `{}` on a response that does not report tiers. When nothing is `active`, `pending` means that an application or enrollment is under review, or that what Anthropic approved does not yet apply to this profile, and `rejected` means that the application or enrollment was declined.

tiers.description: The program's tiers, keyed by tier: `a` (Specialized Access), `b` (Red Team Access) and `c` (Defense Access). A response reports either every tier or none. When it reports them, as retrieving the profile normally does, every tier has a key, whether or not it applies to the profile. When it does not, as in the list of user profiles, `tiers` is `{}`, which does not mean that the tiers are inactive. No tier implies another, so read the tier you need. Anthropic may add tiers; ignore a key you do not recognize.

requirements.description: What a request that names the profile must allow to get the relaxed safeguards of every `active` tier. `null` when no tier is `active`, and wherever `tiers` is `{}`.

UserProfileCyberRequirements.description: What a request that names the profile must allow to get the relaxed safeguards of the profile's `active` tiers. A field reads `true` when at least one of those tiers has the requirement and Anthropic has not waived it on that tier for the profile. A request that does not meet a requirement is still served, without the relaxed safeguards of the tiers that have it. The values differ between profiles and can change, so read them rather than assuming them.

data_retention.description: Whether Anthropic must be able to retain the request's inference data.

human_review.description: Whether Anthropic personnel must be allowed to review the data retained from the request.

UserProfileCyberTier.description: One tier of the Cyber Verification Program.

status.description: `active` when the tier applies to the profile, otherwise `inactive`. The response does not say why a tier is `inactive`: it can be in review, declined, withdrawn, never applied for, or approved but not applied to this profile.

UserProfileEfsFeature.description: One feature of Enterprise Frontier Safeguards.

status.description: `active` when Anthropic has approved the entity the profile represents to use the feature, otherwise `inactive`. `active` does not mean that the feature is set up or switched on, which is a separate step.

UserProfileEfsProgram.description: A user profile's standing in Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, a program under which Anthropic approves the entity the profile represents and may approve any of the program's features.

status.description: Anthropic's decision on the entity the profile represents: `pending` while it is awaited, `active` once Anthropic has approved the entity for the program, or `rejected` once Anthropic has declined or has removed the entity from the program. `active` does not mean that any one feature is approved: read the feature you need in `features`.

features.description: The program's features, keyed by feature: `data_retention_exemption` (use of models that normally require data retention, without the data being retained), `cmek` (customer-managed encryption keys) and `storage` (customer-owned storage). Every feature that the caller's organization may read has a key, whether or not it is approved; a missing key does not mean that the feature is inactive. Anthropic may add features; ignore a key you do not recognize.

UserProfileEnforcementAction.description: A limit Anthropic has placed on the entity this profile represents and not yet resolved, discriminated by `type`: `restriction` or `ban`. More types may be added; read a `type` you do not recognize as `restriction`.

UserProfileEnforcementActionBan.description: Anthropic has stopped serving the end user where the ban applies and does not plan to serve them there again.

id.description: The action's ID (`enac_...`), stable while the action is open.

reason.description: Why Anthropic placed the limit: `unsupported_region`, `fraud_or_abuse`, `high_harm`, `usage_policy_violation`, `account_compromise` or `unspecified`.

action.description: Always `null`: the end user cannot clear a ban.

opened_at.description: When Anthropic opened the action, in RFC 3339 format.

expires_at.description: Always `null`: a ban has no end date.

UserProfileEnforcementActionNextStep.description: The next step on this enforcement action: `verify` means the end user can clear the action by passing an identity check. More values may be added; read a value you do not recognize as `null`.

UserProfileEnforcementActionReason.description: Why Anthropic placed this enforcement action: `unsupported_region`, `fraud_or_abuse`, `high_harm`, `usage_policy_violation`, `account_compromise` or `unspecified`. More values may be added; read a value you do not recognize as `unspecified`.

UserProfileEnforcementActionRestriction.description: Anthropic has limited how it serves the end user until the action is resolved. The end user may still be served in part.

id.description: The action's ID (`enac_...`), stable while the action is open.

reason.description: Why Anthropic placed the limit: `unsupported_region`, `fraud_or_abuse`, `high_harm`, `usage_policy_violation`, `account_compromise` or `unspecified`.

action.description: The next step on the action: `verify` or `null`. `verify`: the end user can clear it now by passing an identity check. `null`: there is nothing the end user can do now to clear it, including while Anthropic reviews an identity check the end user submitted.

opened_at.description: When Anthropic opened the action, in RFC 3339 format.

expires_at.description: When the action ends on its own, in RFC 3339 format; it stops showing once this time has passed. `null` when it has no end date, and always `null` when `reason` is `account_compromise`.

UserProfileEnforcementStatus.description: Anthropic's enforcement status of this profile: `unrestricted`, `pending`, `restricted` or `banned`. More values may be added; read a value you do not recognize as `restricted`.

UserProfileEnrollEndUserAction.description: The end-user that the profile represents enrolls in a program.

UserProfileExternalUserAccountStatus.description: The status of the entity's account on the platform, as the platform states it: `active`; `suspended`, when the platform has restricted the account and may restore it; or `blocked`, when the platform has barred it. It records the platform's decision only. The statuses that Anthropic itself reports for the profile, such as its status in a program, are Anthropic's decisions and do not change with it.
x-enum-descriptions: The platform has neither restricted nor barred the account of the entity that the user profile represents.
The platform has restricted the account of the entity that the user profile represents and may restore it.
The platform has barred the account of the entity that the user profile represents.

UserProfileExternalUserDetails.description: Details about the entity this profile represents, as the platform states them. Anthropic does not verify them. Every field is present, `null` until the platform supplies a value.

reference_id.description: The platform's own reference for the entity. `null` until the platform supplies one.

onboarded_at.description: When the entity opened its account with the platform, as stated by the platform, in RFC 3339 format (UTC). `null` until the platform supplies one.

account_status.description: The status of the entity's account on the platform: `active`, `suspended` or `blocked`. `null` until the platform supplies one.

entity_type.description: What kind of entity the profile represents: `individual`, `business`, `non_profit` or `government`. `null` until the platform supplies one.

country.description: The country the platform associates with the entity, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. `null` until the platform supplies one.

name_hash.description: The platform-computed hash of the entity's name. `null` until the platform supplies one.

email_hash.description: The platform-computed hash of the entity's email address. `null` until the platform supplies one.

reference_id.description: The platform's own reference for the entity, for example the key of the end-user's row in the platform's database. Not interpreted by Anthropic and not enforced unique. 1 to 255 characters.

onboarded_at.description: When the entity opened its account with the platform, in RFC 3339 format: for an `application` profile, when the end-user signed up; for a `passthrough` profile, when the company became the platform's customer. Must be a complete timestamp no more than 1 minute in the future.

account_status.description: The status of the entity's account on the platform: `active`, `suspended` or `blocked`.

entity_type.description: What kind of entity the profile represents: `individual`, `business`, `non_profit` or `government`.

country.description: The country of the entity (not of the platform), as the platform determines it: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in upper case, for example `US`. Only the form, two uppercase ASCII letters, is checked.

name_hash.description: A hash of the entity's name, computed by the platform. Anthropic treats it as an opaque string and does not prescribe the hash function. 1 to 255 characters.

email_hash.description: A hash of the entity's email address, computed by the platform. Anthropic treats it as an opaque string and does not prescribe the hash function. 1 to 255 characters.

UserProfileExternalUserEntityType.description: What kind of entity the profile represents, as the platform states it: `individual`, `business`, `non_profit` or `government`.

UserProfileListOrder.description: The direction that a list of user profiles is sorted in.
x-enum-descriptions: Oldest first when `order_by` is `created_at`, or names in ascending order when `order_by` is `name`.
Newest first when `order_by` is `created_at`, or names in descending order when `order_by` is `name`. This is the default.

UserProfileListOrderBy.description: Sort field for listing user profiles: `created_at` (default) or `name` (case-insensitive; profiles without a name sort last).
x-enum-descriptions: Sort by when each user profile was created. This is the default.
Sort by `name`, ignoring the case of ASCII letters. Profiles without a name come last in either direction.

UserProfileProgramStatus.description: A user profile's status in a program. Each program's `status` field says what the values mean there.
x-enum-descriptions: The profile is in the program.
The profile is not in the program yet, and something is still awaited.
The profile is not in the program and nothing is awaited: Anthropic has declined, or has withdrawn an earlier approval.

UserProfilePrograms.description: A user profile's standing in each program. A program is a set of capabilities or exemptions that Anthropic approves for the entity the profile represents. A program reads `null` when the profile has no status in it, when the caller's organization is not entitled to read programs, or when the response does not report that program. Retrieving the profile reports every program. Anthropic may add programs; ignore a key you do not recognize.

cyber.description: The profile's standing in the Cyber Verification Program. `null` when the profile has no status in it. Only retrieving the profile gives the full answer: a list or update response can show `null`, or a status other than `active`, for a profile that reads `active` when retrieved.

efs.description: The profile's standing in Enterprise Frontier Safeguards. `null` unless the platform's attestation for the program is in place on this profile, or the entity it represents has applied to the program. A list of user profiles does not report this program: there it reads `null` for every profile, so retrieve the profile to read it.

BetaAnalyticsArtifactActivity.title: AnalyticsArtifactActivity
BetaAnalyticsArtifactActivity.description:
Artifact-creation activity for one (`artifact_type`, `is_shared`) bucket
on a given day.

Artifacts form a small finite cube — the canonical MIME type (8 values incl.
`other`) crossed with shared-vs-private — so the response is the full set of
non-empty buckets, not a ranked/paginated list. Claude Code and Cowork
artifacts report under `text/html` and are counted from 2026-08-17
onward; earlier days contain claude.ai chat artifacts only. With
`group_by[]=product` / `user_id` / `rbac_group_id` each row is further
split by the flat group keys and counts are scoped to that cut.

next_page.title: Next Page
next_page.description: Cursor for the next page of a grouped query; always null for the ungrouped artifact-type cube, which is returned in full.

BetaAnalyticsArtifactsResponse.title: AnalyticsArtifactsResponse
BetaAnalyticsArtifactsResponse.description:
Response for GET /v1/organizations/analytics/artifacts.

`next_page` is null on ungrouped queries — the artifact-type cube is
finite and returned in full. Grouped queries (`group_by[]` on `product` /
`user_id` / `rbac_group_id`) multiply the cube and paginate like the other
analytics list endpoints.

chat_cowork_unified_metrics.description: Connector use recorded while members had Chat and Cowork unified (Cowork's features inside claude.ai chat) turned on, split into chat conversations and Cowork sessions. A count is null in date-range mode where it cannot be computed. Omitted from the response on deployments that do not offer Chat and Cowork unified.

connector_display_name.title: Connector Display Name
connector_display_name.description: Human-readable display name for rows whose `connector_name` is an opaque connector id rather than a readable name, resolved at request time from the organization's connectors (including connectors that have since been removed). `connector_name` remains the row's stable key for sorting and pagination, and `filter[]=connector_name:{value}` also matches these rows by display name. Display names are not unique, and the same connector's claude.ai usage can appear under a separate row with a readable `connector_name`. Null when `connector_name` is already a readable name, when the id cannot be resolved to one of the organization's connectors, or when display-name resolution is not enabled for this organization.

connector_name.title: Connector Name
connector_name.description: Name of the connector. Some rows carry an opaque connector id here instead of a readable name; `connector_display_name` holds the resolved name for those rows.

distinct_user_count.title: Distinct User Count
distinct_user_count.description: Number of distinct users who used the connector on the requested day, or, in date-range mode, over the requested window — recomputed as an exact distinct count over the window's per-member daily rows, never a sum of per-day values.

individual_auth_distinct_user_count.title: Individual Auth Distinct User Count
individual_auth_distinct_user_count.description: Number of distinct users whose use of this connector on the requested day ran on their own individual credential, connected through their own consent flow. Companion bucket to `managed_auth_distinct_user_count`, which carries the measurement, attribution, and null rules. Users whose requests used no stored credential count in neither bucket.

managed_auth_distinct_user_count.title: Managed Auth Distinct User Count
managed_auth_distinct_user_count.description: Number of distinct users whose use of this connector on the requested day ran on Enterprise Managed Auth (an organization-managed credential provisioned through the organization's identity provider), read from the token record each request used. Null, never 0, when managed-auth reporting is not enabled for the organization, the value cannot be attributed to the row, no credentialed requests and no managed-token mint events (a managed credential being provisioned for a user's use of the connector) were observed that day, or the day predates 2026-07-01, the first day the backing data exists (forward-only data, no backfill). When credentialed requests or mint events were observed and attributed, both managed-auth fields populate, reporting 0 for a bucket with no users; the two counts are independent, not a partition — a user whose requests that day used both kinds of credential counts in both. Mint events carry user but not surface attribution, so they count as observed auth activity on `user_id` and `rbac_group_id` cuts — attributed to the user the credential was provisioned for — but never on a cut that references `product` (group or filter). Date-range rollup mode (`starting_date`/`ending_date`) computes both fields exactly over the window — distinct users with at least one qualifying day — when the whole window starts on or after 2026-07-01, with the null-versus-0 and mint-event rules applying with the window in place of the day; a range starting earlier reports every managed-auth field as null, never a partial-window value.

product.title: Product
product.description: Product that produced this row's activity: one of `chat`, `claude_code`, `cowork`, `office_agent`, or `chat_cowork_unified` (Chat and Cowork unified). These are the canonical Cost & Usage product names; an `office_agent` row's per-surface breakdown is in its `office_metrics`. On `/plugins` only `cowork`, `claude_code` and `chat_cowork_unified` occur (the only surfaces with plugin attribution); on `/artifacts` only `chat`, `claude_code`, `cowork` and `chat_cowork_unified` occur (the surfaces that create artifacts); `/apps/chat/projects` does not support the product dimension (a `product` entry in `group_by[]` or `filter[]` there is rejected). Present only when the request grouped by `product`.

rbac_group_id.title: Rbac Group Id
rbac_group_id.description: Tagged RBAC group identifier (`rbac_group_...`), matching the spend-limits API spelling. Present only when the request grouped by `rbac_group_id`.

rbac_group_name.title: Rbac Group Name
rbac_group_name.description: Resolved RBAC group display name, alongside `rbac_group_id` when name resolution is available. Null if the group has been deleted or its name could not be resolved; `rbac_group_id` remains the stable key.

read_call_count.title: Read Call Count
read_call_count.description: Number of connector tool calls on the requested day whose trusted read-only annotation marked them read-only. Call count, not distinct users. Every call recorded on a classified surface lands in exactly one of `read_call_count`, `write_call_count`, or `unclassified_call_count`, so the three sum to the day's classified calls. Classification is forward-only per surface: claude.ai from 2026-06-01, Claude Code from 2026-05-30, Claude in Office from 2026-05-29, Cowork from 2026-06-02 (Cowork clients predating annotation forwarding land in `unclassified_call_count`). Null, never 0, when the value cannot be stated: the read/write split is not enabled for this organization, or the day predates 2026-05-29. For a date-range total, sum the per-day values, but treat a window that extends before 2026-05-29 as null rather than summing only its covered days — date-range rollup mode (`starting_date`/`ending_date`) applies both rules server-side.

unclassified_call_count.title: Unclassified Call Count
unclassified_call_count.description: Number of connector tool calls on the requested day with no trusted read-only annotation — the annotation is optional in the MCP spec and is discarded when connector access controls are active, so unclassified calls are common. This field shows how much of the day's classified activity the read/write split actually covers. Call count, not distinct users. One of the three call-classification buckets; see `read_call_count` for the per-surface data-start dates, null conditions, and date-range guidance.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: Tagged user identifier (e.g. `user_...`). Present only when the request grouped by `user_id`.

claude_tag_category.description: Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) spend category: `engaged` (a person addressed Claude in a channel or thread), `proactive` (Claude responded without being addressed), `scheduled` (a scheduled routine ran), `monitoring` (Claude watching a channel it was asked to monitor), or `dm` (direct messages with Claude). Populated only when `claude_tag_category` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage that is not Claude Tag. Direct-message usage is billed to the individual user and is reported under that user's product, not under `claude-tag`. New categories may be added over time.

claude_tag_user_id.title: Claude Tag User Id
claude_tag_user_id.description: Slack user ID (for example `U0123ABCDEF`) of the member the Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) usage is attributed to, not a claude.ai user ID. Populated only when `claude_tag_user_id` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage that is not Claude Tag and for Claude Tag usage that is not attributed to a single user (for example `monitoring`, and `proactive` usage Claude initiated), so per-user rows can sum to less than the Claude Tag total. Cannot be combined with `group_by[]=rbac_group_id` or the `rbac_group_ids[]` filter.

context_window.description: Context-window pricing tier of the usage or cost. Null unless `context_window` is in `group_by[]`; it can also be null on grouped rows with no context-window tier, such as code execution.

cost_type.description: Cost component when `group_by[]=cost_type`; null otherwise (amount is the combined total).

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: Currency code for the cost amount. Currently always `"USD"`.

inference_geo.description: Inference region of the usage or cost. Null unless `inference_geo` is in `group_by[]`; it can also be null on grouped rows where the region is not set (the rows that `inference_geos[]=not_available` matches).

model.title: Model
model.description: Model that produced the usage or cost, as a model name in the form the `models[]` filter accepts (for example, `claude-opus-5-5`). Null unless `model` is in `group_by[]`; it can also be null on grouped rows whose usage or cost is not attributed to a specific model, such as code execution.

product.description: Product surface that produced the usage or cost. Null unless product is in `group_by[]`; it can also be null on grouped rows whose usage cannot be attributed to a known surface. Values include `chat`, `claude_code`, `cowork`, `office_agent`, `claude_in_chrome`, `claude_design`, `claude-tag`, and `chat_cowork_unified`. `claude-tag` is Claude Tag, the Claude product in Slack. `chat_cowork_unified` is Chat and Cowork unified, Cowork's features inside claude.ai chat: chat and Cowork usage by a member who has it turned on is reported under this value instead of `chat` or `cowork`. It is accepted as a filter only on deployments that offer Chat and Cowork unified. Some unattributed usage is reported as "other".

rbac_group_id.title: Rbac Group Id
rbac_group_id.description: RBAC group (team) the usage is attributed to, in the public tagged `rbac_group_...` spelling — the same spelling the activity resources use for this key, so the same team has one id across resources and it round-trips as an `rbac_group_ids[]` filter value. Populated only when `rbac_group_id` is in `group_by[]`. Any-membership semantics: a user in several groups contributes their full usage to each of those groups' rows, so the named-group rows overlap and their sum can exceed the org total. A null value is the single unassigned row: users in no group on that (UTC) day. For the true org total, run the same query without `group_by[]`.

requests.title: Requests
requests.description: Number of API requests in this row's scope. Null when `group_by` includes `cost_type` or `token_type` (the count has no per-component attribution; read it from the ungrouped response). For sandbox / code-execution events, this counts execution spans rather than HTTP requests (these rows surface with `product: null`).

slack_channel_id.description: Slack channel the usage originated from. Populated only when `slack_channel_id` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage outside Slack (and for rows recorded before channel attribution was enabled).

speed.description: Inference speed mode of the usage or cost: `fast` or `standard`. Null unless `speed` is in `group_by[]`.

token_type.description: Token type when `group_by[]=token_type` and `cost_type=tokens`; null otherwise.

ending_at.description: End of the time bucket (exclusive) in RFC 3339 format.

workspace_id.title: Workspace Id
workspace_id.description: Workspace the usage occurred in, as a tagged workspace ID, including the organization's default workspace. Populated only when `workspace_id` is in `group_by[]`; null for Claude Enterprise usage.

BetaAnalyticsFlatCostGroup.title: AnalyticsFlatCostGroup
BetaAnalyticsFlatCostGroup.description:
The dimension values one cost row is broken out by, including
`cost_type` and `token_type`.

ending_at.title: Ending At
ending_at.description: End of the period this row covers (exclusive), as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp: the end of the row's time bucket when a time-bucket width is set; otherwise the requested `ending_at` (or, when omitted, the earlier of now and `starting_at` plus 31 days) rounded down to the hour, because without a time bucket the report covers whole hours.

group.description: The dimension values this row's cost is broken out by.

starting_at.title: Starting At
starting_at.description: Start of the period this row covers (inclusive), as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp: the start of the row's time bucket when a time-bucket width is set, otherwise the requested `starting_at` rounded down to the hour.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: Amount (post-discount, pre-credit) in fractional cents (minor units).

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: Currency code for the cost amount. Currently always `"USD"`.

requests.title: Requests
requests.description: Number of API requests in this row's scope. Null when `group_by` includes `cost_type` or `token_type` (the count has no per-component attribution; read it from the ungrouped response). For sandbox / code-execution events, this counts execution spans rather than HTTP requests (these rows surface with `product: null`).

data.title: Data
data.description: Rows for this page, in the order set by `order_by` and `order`: one per combination of the `group_by[]` dimensions (and per time bucket, when `time_bucket_width` is set) with usage or cost in the range, or a single row when neither is set. Rows split out by `cost_type` or `token_type` (cost endpoint only) stay adjacent and are ranked as one unit.

data_refreshed_at.title: Data Refreshed At
data_refreshed_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the export this response was served from. Null when no export yet covers any part of the requested range, in which case `data` is empty. Data beyond this watermark is incomplete; for stable results, set `ending_at` to this value or earlier. Data is typically refreshed every 4 hours. Values can be revised as late events arrive and reconciliation runs, until about 7 days after the end of the calendar month the usage falls in; for example, values for October 1 can change until about November 7.

has_more.title: Has More
has_more.description: Whether another page is available. When true, pass `next_page` as the `page` parameter to fetch it.

next_page.title: Next Page
next_page.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null when `has_more` is false. Pass it as the `page` parameter, keeping the other parameters unchanged. A cursor can expire after the underlying data refreshes; the request then returns HTTP 410 and pagination must restart from the first page.

actor.description: The identity the usage is attributed to: the user if one is attributed, else the service account, else the federated (cloud-platform) identity, else the API key. Populated only when `actor` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage with no attributable identity, and for users' and federated identities' usage when the reader is a member who can see only some workspaces. Distinct identities the server cannot render also read null, each as its own row.

actor_type.description: Kind of identity the usage is attributed to; matches `actor.type` when `actor` is set. Populated only when `actor_type` is in `group_by[]`.

agent_id.title: Agent Id
agent_id.description: Claude Managed Agents agent whose session incurred the usage. Populated only when `agent_id` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage outside a managed session.

api_key_id.title: Api Key Id
api_key_id.description: API key that authenticated the requests, as a tagged API key ID, whichever identity `actor` resolves to. Populated only when `api_key_id` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage not authenticated by an API key.

claude_tag_category.description: Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) spend category: `engaged` (a person addressed Claude in a channel or thread), `proactive` (Claude responded without being addressed), `scheduled` (a scheduled routine ran), `monitoring` (Claude watching a channel it was asked to monitor), or `dm` (direct messages with Claude). Populated only when `claude_tag_category` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage that is not Claude Tag. Direct-message usage is billed to the individual user and is reported under that user's product, not under `claude_tag`. New categories may be added over time.

claude_tag_user_id.title: Claude Tag User Id
claude_tag_user_id.description: Slack user ID (for example `U0123ABCDEF`) of the member the Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) usage is attributed to, not a claude.ai user ID. Populated only when `claude_tag_user_id` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage that is not Claude Tag and for Claude Tag usage that is not attributed to a single user (for example `monitoring`, and `proactive` usage Claude initiated), so per-user rows can sum to less than the Claude Tag total. Cannot be combined with `group_by[]=rbac_group_id` or the `rbac_group_ids[]` filter.

context_window.description: Context-window pricing tier of the usage or cost. Null unless `context_window` is in `group_by[]`; it can also be null on grouped rows with no context-window tier, such as code execution.

deployment_id.title: Deployment Id
deployment_id.description: Deployment that started the Claude Managed Agents session. Populated only when `deployment_id` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage outside a managed session and for sessions no deployment started.

environment_id.title: Environment Id
environment_id.description: Claude Managed Agents environment the session ran in. Populated only when `environment_id` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage outside a managed session.

inference_geo.description: Inference region of the usage or cost. Null unless `inference_geo` is in `group_by[]`; it can also be null on grouped rows where the region is not set (the rows that `inference_geos[]=not_available` matches).

model.title: Model
model.description: Model that produced the usage or cost, as a model name in the form the `models[]` filter accepts (for example, `claude-opus-5-5`). Null unless `model` is in `group_by[]`; it can also be null on grouped rows whose usage or cost is not attributed to a specific model, such as code execution.

product.description: Product surface that produced the usage or cost. Null unless product is in `group_by[]`; it can also be null on grouped rows whose usage cannot be attributed to a known surface. Values include `chat`, `claude_code`, `cowork`, `office_agent`, `claude_in_chrome`, `claude_design`, `claude_tag`, and `chat_cowork_unified`. `claude_tag` is Claude Tag, the Claude product in Slack. `chat_cowork_unified` is Chat and Cowork unified, Cowork's features inside claude.ai chat: chat and Cowork usage by a member who has it turned on is reported under this value instead of `chat` or `cowork`. It is accepted as a filter only on deployments that offer Chat and Cowork unified. Some unattributed usage is reported as "other".

rbac_group_id.title: Rbac Group Id
rbac_group_id.description: RBAC group (team) the usage is attributed to, in the public tagged `rbac_group_...` spelling — the same spelling the activity resources use for this key, so the same team has one id across resources and it round-trips as an `rbac_group_ids[]` filter value. Populated only when `rbac_group_id` is in `group_by[]`. Any-membership semantics: a user in several groups contributes their full usage to each of those groups' rows, so the named-group rows overlap and their sum can exceed the org total. A null value is the single unassigned row: users in no group on that (UTC) day. For the true org total, run the same query without `group_by[]`.

service_tier.description: Service tier the usage was served at. Populated only when `service_tier` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage with no service tier (for example, code execution) and for Claude Enterprise usage.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Claude Managed Agents session that incurred the usage. Populated only when `session_id` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage outside a managed session.

slack_channel_id.title: Slack Channel Id
slack_channel_id.description: Slack channel the usage originated from. Populated only when `slack_channel_id` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage outside Slack (and for rows recorded before channel attribution was enabled).

speed.description: Inference speed mode of the usage or cost: `fast` or `standard`. Null unless `speed` is in `group_by[]`.

user_profile_id.title: User Profile Id
user_profile_id.description: User profile the usage was attributed to, as a tagged `uprof_` ID. Populated only when `user_profile_id` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage that named no profile and for Claude Enterprise usage.

workspace_id.title: Workspace Id
workspace_id.description: Workspace the usage occurred in, as a tagged workspace ID, including the organization's default workspace. Populated only when `workspace_id` is in `group_by[]`; null for Claude Enterprise usage.

distinct_user_count.title: Distinct User Count
distinct_user_count.description: Number of distinct users with recorded install or invocation activity for the plugin on the requested day (install-only users count), or, in date-range mode, over the requested window — recomputed as an exact distinct count over the window's per-member daily rows, never a sum of per-day values.

install_count.title: Install Count
install_count.description: Number of distinct users who installed the plugin on the requested day, or, in date-range mode, over the requested window — recomputed as an exact distinct count over the window's per-member daily rows, never a sum of per-day values.

invocation_count.title: Invocation Count
invocation_count.description: Number of plugin invocations on the requested day

plugin_id.title: Plugin Id
plugin_id.description: Stable plugin identifier when available (e.g. `serena@claude-plugins-official`). Null for third-party Claude Code plugins (redacted at the source) and Cowork slash commands that carry only a hashed id.

product.title: Product
product.description: Product that produced this row's activity: one of `chat`, `claude_code`, `cowork`, `office_agent`, or `chat_cowork_unified` (Chat and Cowork unified). These are the canonical Cost & Usage product names; an `office_agent` row's per-surface breakdown is in its `office_metrics`. On `/plugins` only `cowork`, `claude_code` and `chat_cowork_unified` occur (the only surfaces with plugin attribution); on `/artifacts` only `chat`, `claude_code`, `cowork` and `chat_cowork_unified` occur (the surfaces that create artifacts); `/apps/chat/projects` does not support the product dimension (a `product` entry in `group_by[]` or `filter[]` there is rejected). Present only when the request grouped by `product`.

rbac_group_name.title: Rbac Group Name

user_id.title: User Id

Omitted from the response while the per-product breakdown is not enabled for this organization.

science_weekly_active_user_count.title: Science Weekly Active User Count

starting_at.title: Starting At

weekly_active_user_count.title: Weekly Active User Count

weekly_adoption_rate.title: Weekly Adoption Rate

attributed_list_price.title: Attributed List Price
attributed_list_price.description: List-price (rate-card) value of the member requests attributed to this skill, as a decimal string in the minor unit of `currency` (cents for USD), from Claude Code, Cowork, and Office Agent request-level attribution — the value of requests that involved the skill, not the skill's incremental cost. Unlike `estimated_overage_spend` this reflects usage value regardless of how it was funded — seat-covered usage counts — but it is undiscounted and does not tie to billed spend or the organization's spend reporting. claude.ai chat usage carries no request-level attribution and contributes nothing: the field is null on `chat` product rows and on `office_agent` product cuts dated before 2026-06-18 (the Office Agent attribution data-start), and on ungrouped rows it covers the Claude Code + Cowork + Office Agent share only (null when no attributable usage exists). Also null under the same conditions as `estimated_overage_spend` (spend reporting not enabled for this organization, `office_agent` product cuts before the 2026-06-18 data-start). "0" means attributable usage existed but none was attributed to this skill. Addable across days: date-range rollup mode returns the window's sum. On `group_by[]` and `filter[]` shapes both amounts can total below the ungrouped value for the same skill over the same date or range: spend attributed to a member–skill pair with no counted usage on that day is excluded from those cuts.

chat_cowork_unified_metrics.description: Skill use recorded while members had Chat and Cowork unified (Cowork's features inside claude.ai chat) turned on, split into chat conversations and Cowork sessions. A count is null in date-range mode where it cannot be computed. Omitted from the response on deployments that do not offer Chat and Cowork unified.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: Currency for this row's monetary fields (`estimated_overage_spend` and `attributed_list_price`), as an uppercase ISO-4217 code. Always "USD" when either amount is populated; null whenever both amounts are null.

distinct_user_count.title: Distinct User Count
distinct_user_count.description: Number of distinct users who used the skill on the requested day, or, in date-range mode, over the requested window — recomputed as an exact distinct count over the window's per-member daily rows, never a sum of per-day values. A skill counts as used only when it is explicitly activated — the model (or the user, via the skill's slash command) invokes it, reading its instructions into context as part of that activation. Skills that are merely installed or listed as available, or whose content reaches the context without an activation (preloaded, hook-injected, or read as a plain file), are not counted.

enable_count.title: Enable Count
enable_count.description: Distinct accounts that enabled this skill on the requested day (claude.ai only — the skill analog of plugin `install_count`). The count is org-wide: null when enable reporting is not enabled for this organization, or when the request scopes to `user_id` / `rbac_group_id` / `product` via `group_by[]` or `filter[]` (an org-wide count would be misleading on per-cut rows). A distinct count, not an event count: summing across days double-counts members who enable the skill on more than one day, so it is also null in date-range rollup mode (`starting_date`/`ending_date`).

estimated_overage_spend.title: Estimated Overage Spend
estimated_overage_spend.description: Estimated overage spend attributed to this skill, as a decimal string in the minor unit of `currency` (cents for USD; "1250" is $12.50, fractional cents possible) — an allocation of each member's daily post-discount, pre-credit metered overage spend (the same cost basis as the organization's spend reporting and the Cost & Usage API, so per-skill figures are directly comparable; spend with no skill attribution — including any member-day without skill invocations — is not represented, so skill rows sum to at most those totals) across the skills the member used. Overage only: usage covered by included seat allowances bills nothing and allocates $0 here — see `attributed_list_price` for the funding-independent usage-value companion. Claude Code, Cowork, and Office Agent spend use request-level skill attribution; claude.ai chat spend is approximated proportionally to skill-invoking messages. An estimate, not a billing number — and the cost of the requests/messages that involved the skill, not the skill's incremental cost (the same request would still have cost something without the skill active). "0" means no overage spend was attributed; null when spend reporting is not enabled for this organization, on `office_agent` product cuts dated before 2026-06-18 (the Office Agent attribution data-start). Addable across days: date-range rollup mode (`starting_date`/`ending_date`) returns the window's sum. With `group_by[]=user_id` each row carries the user's own attributed spend. On `group_by[]` and `filter[]` shapes both amounts can total below the ungrouped value for the same skill over the same date or range: spend attributed to a member–skill pair with no counted usage on that day is excluded from those cuts.

invocation_count.title: Invocation Count
invocation_count.description: Total number of times this skill was invoked on the requested day (the skill analog of plugin `invocation_count`). Unlike `distinct_user_count` — which answers '# of users' — this is the true '# of uses'. A skill counts as used only when it is explicitly activated — the model (or the user, via the skill's slash command) invokes it, reading its instructions into context as part of that activation. Skills that are merely installed or listed as available, or whose content reaches the context without an activation (preloaded, hook-injected, or read as a plain file), are not counted. Null when invocation reporting is not enabled for this organization. Sum across a date range for total uses in the window — date-range rollup mode (`starting_date`/`ending_date`) returns this sum directly.

product.title: Product
product.description: Product that produced this row's activity: one of `chat`, `claude_code`, `cowork`, `office_agent`, or `chat_cowork_unified` (Chat and Cowork unified). These are the canonical Cost & Usage product names; an `office_agent` row's per-surface breakdown is in its `office_metrics`. On `/plugins` only `cowork`, `claude_code` and `chat_cowork_unified` occur (the only surfaces with plugin attribution); on `/artifacts` only `chat`, `claude_code`, `cowork` and `chat_cowork_unified` occur (the surfaces that create artifacts); `/apps/chat/projects` does not support the product dimension (a `product` entry in `group_by[]` or `filter[]` there is rejected). Present only when the request grouped by `product`.

rbac_group_id.title: Rbac Group Id
rbac_group_id.description: Tagged RBAC group identifier (`rbac_group_...`), matching the spend-limits API spelling. Present only when the request grouped by `rbac_group_id`.

rbac_group_name.title: Rbac Group Name
rbac_group_name.description: Resolved RBAC group display name, alongside `rbac_group_id` when name resolution is available. Null if the group has been deleted or its name could not be resolved; `rbac_group_id` remains the stable key.

share_status.title: Share Status
share_status.description: Skill share status (claude.ai only): one of `private`, `organization`, or `public`. Null for skills used only in Claude Code or Office (no per-skill share-status concept) and when share-status reporting is not yet available for the organization. Filterable via `filter[]=share_status:{value}`.

skill_display_name.title: Skill Display Name
skill_display_name.description: Human-readable display name for rows whose `skill_name` is an opaque skill id (user/organization skill types and plugin-delivered skills, whose user-defined names usage reports generally withhold). Organization-shared skills and skills delivered by the organization's own plugins (its plugin marketplaces and its library) resolve; plugin skill names are shown without their 'plugin:' prefix. The literal 'unknown' bucket row gets a fixed 'Unknown skill' label. For a member's own skill (private or personal-plugin) it is null, except when the skill's owner used it from Claude Code or Cowork in the requested period: then it shows the name that client reported at the time. Apart from that, the names of members' own skills are not disclosed to analytics-key holders. Also null for Anthropic-provided plugin skills (not resolved), for an organization skill or plugin whose name can no longer be found (for example, one since deleted), when `skill_name` is already a display name, or when display-name resolution is not enabled for this organization.

user_id.description: Tagged user identifier (e.g. `user_...`). Present only when the request grouped by `user_id`.

Buckets beyond this watermark are incomplete; for stable results, set `ending_at` to this value or earlier. Data is typically refreshed every 4 hours. Values can be revised as late events arrive and reconciliation runs, until about 7 days after the end of the calendar month the usage falls in; for example, values for October 1 can change until about November 7.

claude_tag_category.description: Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) spend category: `engaged` (a person addressed Claude in a channel or thread), `proactive` (Claude responded without being addressed), `scheduled` (a scheduled routine ran), `monitoring` (Claude watching a channel it was asked to monitor), or `dm` (direct messages with Claude). Populated only when `claude_tag_category` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage that is not Claude Tag. Direct-message usage is billed to the individual user and is reported under that user's product, not under `claude-tag`. New categories may be added over time.

claude_tag_user_id.description: Slack user ID (for example `U0123ABCDEF`) of the member the Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) usage is attributed to, not a claude.ai user ID. Populated only when `claude_tag_user_id` is in `group_by[]`; null for usage that is not Claude Tag and for Claude Tag usage that is not attributed to a single user (for example `monitoring`, and `proactive` usage Claude initiated), so per-user rows can sum to less than the Claude Tag total. context_window.description: Context-window pricing tier of the usage or cost. Null unless `context_window` is in `group_by[]`; it can also be null on grouped rows with no context-window tier, such as code execution.

inference_geo.description: Inference region of the usage or cost. Null unless `inference_geo` is in `group_by[]`; it can also be null on grouped rows where the region is not set (the rows that `inference_geos[]=not_available` matches).

model.title: Model
model.description: Model that produced the usage or cost, as a model name in the form the `models[]` filter accepts (for example, `claude-opus-5-5`). Null unless `model` is in `group_by[]`; it can also be null on grouped rows whose usage or cost is not attributed to a specific model, such as code execution.

output_tokens.description: The number of output tokens generated.

product.description: Product surface that produced the usage or cost. Null unless product is in `group_by[]`; it can also be null on grouped rows whose usage cannot be attributed to a known surface. Values include `chat`, `claude_code`, `cowork`, `office_agent`, `claude_in_chrome`, `claude_design`, `claude-tag`, and `chat_cowork_unified`. `claude-tag` is Claude Tag, the Claude product in Slack. `chat_cowork_unified` is Chat and Cowork unified, Cowork's features inside claude.ai chat: chat and Cowork usage by a member who has it turned on is reported under this value instead of `chat` or `cowork`. It is accepted as a filter only on deployments that offer Chat and Cowork unified. Some unattributed usage is reported as "other".

Populated only when `rbac_group_id` is in `group_by[]`. Any-membership semantics: a user in several groups contributes their full usage to each of those groups' rows, so the named-group rows overlap and their sum can exceed the org total. A null value is the single unassigned row: users in no group on that (UTC) day. For the true org total, run the same query without `group_by[]`.

In date-range mode, recomputed as an exact distinct count of the group's active members over the requested window, never a sum of per-day values.

last_activity_date.title: Last Activity Date
last_activity_date.description: Most recent UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD) on which the user had any counted activity, within the requested window: equal to the requested `date` in single-day mode, and to the latest active day from `starting_date` (inclusive) to `ending_date` (exclusive) in date-range rollup mode — never a day earlier than the window start. On filtered requests (`filter[]`) only days matching the filter count: with `filter[]=rbac_group_id:{id}` it is the last day the user was active while a member of that group, consistent with the row's other metrics. On grouped (`group_by[]`) rows it is the latest day any member of the group was active (the requested `date` in single-day mode). Omitted from the response while last-activity reporting is not enabled for this organization.

name.description: Lowercase identifier, unique within its plugin marketplace. Fixed for an organization-owned Plugin's lifetime; a member-owned Plugin's changes when its owner renames it in claude.ai, while its `id` stays the same.

organization_installation_preference.title: Organization Installation Preference
organization_installation_preference.description: Organization-owned Plugin: the organization-wide installation setting every member gets unless an RBAC Group they belong to holds its own — the Plugin's own setting, or its plugin marketplace's default. Null for a member-owned Plugin, which has shares instead. One of `required`, `auto_install`, `available`, `not_available`; a value this API does not yet name is returned as stored.

organization_installation_preference_inh.title: Organization Installation Preference Inherited
organization_installation_preference_inh.description: Organization-owned Plugin: true while it has no organization-wide setting of its own and `organization_installation_preference` is its plugin marketplace's default. Null for a member-owned Plugin.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Who owns the Plugin: the organization, or the member whose personal plugin marketplace it lives in.

reach.title: Reach
reach.description:
How far the served version reaches, or `null` if it is not classified.

`remote` means it declares an MCP server or a CLI. `privileged` means it declares no MCP server or CLI, but declares a hook, monitor, language server, or settings, or has a skill, command, or other Markdown file whose frontmatter pre-approves tools (`allowed-tools` with any value other than an empty one or one that names only `AskUserQuestion`, `TodoWrite`, and `ToolSearch`). Otherwise it is `contained`.

If the frontmatter of a skill, command, or other Markdown file that could change the value could not be read, or was past a size limit, the version is `null` or `privileged` (or `remote`, if it declares an MCP server or a CLI), not `contained`. The value is normally worked out when a version is stored, under the rules of that time, so an older version can be `null`, or `contained` where the same files stored today would be `privileged` or `null`.

served_version_id.title: Served Version Id
served_version_id.description: The version claude.ai serves to members.

served_version_pinned.title: Served Version Pinned
served_version_pinned.description: True once the served version has been pinned, through Update Plugin or in claude.ai. While false, a new version normally becomes the served version when it is stored. While the newest version is not the served version, as when a version saved in claude.ai is waiting for its content scan, `served_version_id` differs from `latest_version_id`.

type.title: Type
type.description: Always `plugin`.

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: RFC 3339. Moves on a served-version change (including pinning an unpinned Plugin to the version it already serves) and, normally, on a new version. A version saved in claude.ai that waits for its content scan moves it when it becomes the served version, and not necessarily when it is stored. A change to the Plugin's installation settings or shares does not move it.
